value.rationale: For an infinite naturally parametrized family of nonassociative algebras, square-zero existence and its precise count are intrinsic algebraic questions not settled by generic zero-divisor existence or idempotent results. The result exhibits a sharp number-theoretic criterion (-2 in <q> modulo p), including a binary-field parity dichotomy; the weighted polynomial simultaneously determines every square-zero count and shows striking arithmetic changes (e.g. (5,2):1 versus (5,4):31). A complete exact finite-field enumerator is useful for studying zero-square loci and separating coefficient-field behavior. It is not a mere unmotivated single parameter computation.
